headline: Council approves $735,000 for winter warming shelter at 166 Riverside Industrial Parkway, rejects Homeless Services Center expansion.
summary: The shelter money comes from the opioid settlement fund. Staff said the 166 Riverside shelter can open only as fast as it hires and trains staff. Staff said the Homeless Services Center option could open by December 15th. A 20-year extension of the Northeast Air ground lease also passed.
decisions: Approved raising the business assistance grant from $10,000 to $20,000, unanimously.
Denied the motion to postpone the 54 Danforth Street license to November 16th, 4-5.
Approved catering with outdoor dining and combined entertainment at 54 Danforth Street, unanimously.
Approved the Class 1 FSE application without door dining at 476 Stevens, unanimously.
Approved changing the Lancaster Street commercial loading zone to a one-hour zone that Portland High School students can park in, unanimously.
Approved the administrative fee increase for parking in the First Light Commons lots, unanimously.
Approved an option to extend the Northeast Air ground lease by 20 years, with a hangar replacement of at least $4 million, unanimously.
Approved the purchase and sale agreement between Nordic main LLC and Portland for Portland Technology Park units 3 & 5, unanimously.
Approved a salary increase for the Corporation Council, unanimously.
Denied, 4-5, the emergency order to expand the winter warming shelter at the Homeless Services Center.
Approved an amendment setting the 166 Riverside Industrial Parkway shelter amount at $735,000, 9-0.
Approved $735,000 from the opioid settlement fund for a winter warming shelter at 166 Riverside Industrial Parkway, 8-1, as amended.
Postponed indefinitely the $350,000 appropriation from the opioid settlement fund for the emergency winter warming shelter.
discussion: Winter warming shelter location: Members weighed the Homeless Services Center against 166 Riverside Industrial Parkway. Staff said 52 people are under trespass orders for the shelter and cannot stay there, and that a site at 166 Riverside could take longer to open.

Opioid settlement fund use: Public speakers said the money should go to treatment, recovery, and harm reduction instead of shelter operations. Speakers also said a warming shelter is a basic need, and the city's legal office said the use is allowed.

54 Danforth Street license: Neighbors said doors had been left open during amplified entertainment. The applicant said it would have a staff member keep doors closed and check decibels at events. Members debated postponing the decision to November 16th, and the postponement failed 4-5.
